name: Godhood
description:
If you choose to use this world module, the following is true:

  1. It is part of the nature of magic in your campaign world that a person's devotion carries real, tangible power.

  2. That power gathers and grows in a person who devotes themselves wholly to a particular concept, principle or practice.

  3. That power is further multiplied as they win followers whose own devotional power flows into them.

  4. If this power grows to be great enough, the person achieves godhood over their chosen domain, transcending their mortal form and joining an ever-changing pantheon, populated by others who have achieved godhood.

Domain

Each god holds power and responsibility over a domain. Some domains are grand and far-reaching, such as light, darkness, war, or peace, while others - far more numerous - are humble and/or highly specific: persimmons, sandals, the making of bells, one particular waterfall, rude jokes regarding livestock, the feeling of drinking water after long thirst, joinery, contented silence, etc.

Each god's domain must be unique. The definition of "unique" is up to you and your group. You might choose to allow some overlap (a sea domain does not preclude a tides domain and angling domain) or prefer strict delineations (the existence of a sea domain disallows a tides or angling domain). Discuss as a group and come to a consensus.

Whatever your definition, the following is true:

  1. A person who directs their devotion toward an occupied domain lends power to the god presiding over it.

  2. A person who directs their devotion toward an unoccupied domain begins to collect power within themselves, rising toward godhood over that domain.

That power, collected or given, is represented by a Devotion score:

Devotion

Each god wields explicit mechanical influence in the game, which is defined by their Devotion score.

To calculate a god's Devotion score, you must determine five factors:

  • FOLLOWERS. The number of living mortals who recognize the god's godhood, to one degree or another.

  • FERVOR. The intensity of the followers' recognition of the god. The amount of devotional energy they direct toward the god.

  • INSTITUTIONS. The built places and/or traditions that living mortals devote to the god.

  • REACH. The prevalence of recognition in the world, geographically and culturally.

  • DOMAIN. The prevalence of the god's domain in the world. How foundational is their domain to the ways of the world?

To calculate Devotion:

  1. Choose the most appropriate level for each factor, choosing an average if various levels exist across the world.

  2. Multiply the scores for FOLLOWERS x FERVOR.

  3. Add the scores for INSTITUTIONS, REACH, and DOMAIN to the result.

For example, let us say that there is a god of a particular river. There are approximately 3,000 people living in the river's valley, and they are in the habit of leaving offerings at shrines to the river god on a monthly basis. We would give a FOLLOWERS score of 4 (thousands), a FERVOR score of 3 (regular worship), an INSTITUTIONS score of 10 (public shrines or common traditions), a REACH score of 5 (one community) and a DOMAIN score of 5 (narrow - the god's domain is just one river in a wide world). Thus:

(4 x 3) + 10 +5 + 5 = 32

This score will change over time.

For example, perhaps the river floods and destroys many homes, causing the people to lose faith in the river god. Now most of the people neglect the shrines and only think occasionally of the god, while a few hundred faithful maintain the old ways, with regular offerings. We might now place FOLLOWERS at 3 (hundreds) and FERVOR at 2 - an average of 3 (regular worship) and 1 (nominal recognition). Thus:

(3 x 2) + 10 +5 + 5 = 26

Conversely, let us suppose that gold is discovered in the river and the population booms to 20,000 people. There is now a dedicated temple to the river god, and people make daily offerings. FOLLOWERS is now 5 (tens of thousands), FERVOR is 3 (regular worship) and INSTITUTIONS is now 15 (established temples or omnipresent traditions), while REACH and DOMAIN remain the same. Thus:

(5 x 3) + 15 +5 + 5 = 40

And so on.

Attaining & Losing Godhood

An ordinary person has a Devotion score of 0. A mortal on the path to godhood might have a score somewhere between 1 and 19, depending on the extent of their commitment and followers. When a mortal achieves a Devotion of 20, they achieve godhood, gaining the Godhood ability, which grants them powers proportionate to their current Devotion score. There is no upper limit to a Devotion score, and dropping below the threshold of 20 does not automatically revoke the status of Godhood.

Note that while the Godhood ability grants an infinite lifespan, can be killed - whether through violence, mishap, or their Devotion score dropping to 0 (and thus their base Endurance being multiplied by 0) - at which point they become irrevocably diminished, doomed to wander the world incorporeal and powerless, for all time.

Also note that Devotion is calculated moment-to-moment. For example, if a massive explosion destroys most of a god's devotees, their Devotion score would be immediately reduced to reflect a lower FOLLOWERS score.

Alignment

When a new god takes up their domain, they also take up an alignment, which represents their moral relationship to the world of mortals and the influence of the actions they choose to take:

Any god of any domain can exist in any alignment.

Because each god begins as a mortal being and achieves godhood through the actions they take during their lifetime, their initial alignment should reflect the morality underlying those actions. A god's alignment may shift if, as they use their godly power and influence to shape the world, their actions reflect a different morality.

For example, consider a god of the travel domain who attained godhood with an initial alignment of Lawful Good. Perhaps, over time, some of their devotees take to committing acts of highway robbery and the god chooses not to intervene. Following these events, your group might choose to update the god's alignment to True Neutral as a result. If, later, the god begins to actively aid in the robberies, you might then consider updating their alignment to one of the Evil alignments.

When such an extreme reversal as the above example occurs, you might consider the god's actions to represent an abdication of their original domain (thus leaving an opening for a new god of travel to rise) and/or the assumption of a new domain (thus widening the sphere of their original domain).

These are subjective, moral judgements that you and your group should discuss in order to arrive at consensus. You may choose to take up these discussions in a moment of critical interaction or during an Intermezzo. It is up to the group, not an individual GM, to adjudicate alignment changes.

Alignment Bonus

When multiple gods share an alignment, their moral proximity to one another generates additional power. Divide the total Devotion score of all gods in a given alignment by 10. The result is that alignment's Alignment Bonus. Each god in that alignment may add their Alignment Bonus to their Devotion score for the purpose of calculating the benefits granted by the Godhood ability.

This bonus changes as gods' alignments and Devotion scores change.

Establishing A Pantheon

When using this world module, add a step to the campaign creation process, where you will establish the initial pantheon of gods for your campaign world. You may place this step at any point in the process - before or after you establish a map, before or after you define "The Recent Upheaval," before or after you place cultures - or you may touch upon it throughout the process as the world comes into focus.

There is no "right" or "wrong" number of gods, no "right" or "wrong" distribution of Devotion scores and alignments. The best approach is to simply describe the gods of your campaign world as you would any other part of it, then use the Devotion score tables and alignment chart to determine the mechanical potency of those gods.

Apart from the gods defined by the Votary mestiere (see below) Renaissance also offers no specific gods. It is up to you and your group to invent them and define their domains. If you want your gods to be actively present in your campaign, fill out character sheets for them and apply the Godhood ability. Alternately, you may keep them more abstract, represented only as a Devotion score and alignment.

You may of course choose to create your campaign world with an empty pantheon, allowing the campaign to see the rise of new gods.

The Votary Mestiere

This world module is intended to support the Votary mestiere, allowing characters to interact directly with gods, bear influence upon higher spheres of concern, or even attain godhood themselves.

It is certainly possible to use this world module without including the Votary mestiere in your campaign. It is also possible to include the Votary mestiere without the full Godhood world module, though you would need to establish and track the Devotion scores for each Votary's god in order for that mestiere's mechanics to function.
